dataset.name: Model scripts associated with “Revisiting controls on hyporheic respiration with knowledge-guided machine learning at continental scale”
description: NOTE: The manuscript associated with this data package is currently in review. The data/scripts may be revised based on reviewer feedback. Upon manuscript acceptance, this data package will be updated with the final scripts and additional metadata.

This data package is associated with the publication “Revisiting controls on hyporheic respiration with knowledge-guided machine learning at continental scale” submitted to Environmental Science & Technology (Zheng et al. 2026). The project combines mechanistic process modeling with knowledge-guided machine learning (KGML) to evaluate how organic matter chemistry, microbial biomass, and physical substrate accessibility regulate realized respiration rates across river corridors.

All data used in this paper have been previously published and can be accessed at https://data.ess-dive.lbl.gov/datasets/doi:10.15485/1729719 (Goldman et al., 2020). This data package contains 3 R-markdown (Rmd) preprocessing scripts for the previously published data and subsequent modelling workflows. The full workflow with input and output data can be found in the associated GitHub repository at https://github.com/jianqiuz/KGML-WHONDRS.

measurementTechnique: Hyporheic sediment samples were collected as part of the WHONDRS S19S field campaign across multiple river corridors in North America. Laboratory incubations were conducted to quantify sediment respiration rates under controlled conditions. Microbial biomass, organic matter chemistry, and physical sediment properties were measured using standard biogeochemical and analytical protocols, and site-level metadata were compiled from field observations (details can be accessed via ESS-DIVE: doi:10.15485/1729719).

The dataset supports mechanistic and machine-learning modeling workflows. A process-based respiration model was implemented using thermodynamically informed rate formulations with explicit representation of organic matter chemistry, microbial biomass, and physical substrate accessibility. Knowledge-guided machine learning (KGML) workflows incorporated mechanistic model outputs to structure model inputs and residual learning, supporting reproducible integration of process-based and data-driven methods.
